newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Telinor to focus on local phone market.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Telinor to focus on local phone market.

text.p: Telefonia Inalambrica del Norte (Telinor) has a different strategy than many of its future competitors in Mexico's telephone market.

Whereas industry leaders such as AT&T Corp, MCI Communications Inc and GTE Corp plan to enter the lucrative long-distance market once it is opened up next year, Telinor will focus on local telephone service, using wireless technology as its comparative advantage.

"Everyone talks about how local telephone service is no business. But they are wrong -- the Baby Bells in the United States have operated successfully for years," Reynaldo Villarreal, marketing director for the company, told Reuters in an interview.

Telinor's spending plans are just as ambitious as its more well-known U.S.-based competitors -- $1 billion over five years to set up two million connections for local telephone service. The company says it is looking for a partner to help it reach its spending goal.
Villarreal said Mexico's local telephone market had great potential when compared with other countries with similar gross domestic product per capita, such as Greece.
"Greece has a slightly higher per capital income than Mexico, but it has 50 telephone lines per 100 people, while Mexico has nine (per 100)," he said.

The company has a concession to provide local telephone services once the Mexican market opens to competition on January 1. It is the only company besides the leading Mexican telephone company, Telefonos de Mexico SA, that has a local license.
